## How to read a ticket

`T-###` — title. **Next free number: T-299** — before minting ticket numbers, check this line, the board *and* `git log` (concurrent sessions collided twice: T-208–T-210, T-223–T-233); bump this line in the same commit that claims numbers. **Deps:** tickets that must be done first. **Done when:** the acceptance test, drawn from the walking skeleton's milestone acceptance. Package names from [repo-structure.md](repo-structure.md). A ticket is sized for one focused agent run (roughly a PR each).

**Definition of done, every ticket:** typed against `packages/contracts`; unit-tested; no surface reaches below the API; no code path resolves its own permissions (component 2 rule); lints and builds clean in CI.

---

## ⚠ One named build-time decision — skeleton auth

The design layer defers real identity/security to the infra/security session (component 1, open). The skeleton still needs a login. **Decision taken for the skeleton, to be superseded by that session:** email + password session login for the seeded users (`POST /auth/session`, httpOnly cookie), plus Entra ID SSO on the Copilot path (M6, where Microsoft mandates it). No self-serve signup, no password reset, no roles beyond what the data model already carries. This is scaffolding, not the security model; it is listed here so it is a recorded choice, not an accident.

**Production identity is committed as Entra-first (recorded 2026-07-04):** most users will arrive through Microsoft Entra (Azure AD), so production login is Entra ID SSO (OIDC) as the primary path, with the skeleton's password login retained only as a break-glass/dev mechanism to be decided at the infra/security session. The build already enables this: identity is established at one API boundary only (T-021/T-023, contracts principle 3), `User.external_identity` carries the Entra subject from Drawer 1, and T-071 exercises the full Entra → User → Participant mapping. Adding web SSO later is an additive login route, not a rework.

## The roadmap after the skeleton (coarse — ticketed when its slice starts)

Ordered by the wedge-first logic of the overview; each slice names its design gate from the [grill tracker](../grill-sessions/grill-questions.md). Nothing here is execution-ready by design.

**Slice A3 — Co-authoring & the editing substrate: Infora as a WOPI host, native Office files co-authored in real Microsoft Office** — 🎯 **designed 2026-07-25 (ADR-0043 + amendments to 0034 / 0036 / 0039 / 0041); P1 ticketed (T-220–T-222 — renumbered 2026-07-25: the drafted T-208–T-210 were already taken by Slice S), P2–P4 coarse until the CSPP / engine track is live.** The sandbox becomes a true SharePoint / iManage-style working area: drop a draft, open it in Word / Excel / PowerPoint, co-author, and have edits sync straight back — files never leaving Infora. The incumbent-validated posture (iManage Work co-authoring; NetDocuments CollabSpaces — both keep files in their own DMS and become WOPI hosts, renting Office co-authoring via Microsoft's CSPP). Infora stays the system of record and the ethical-wall authority; the SharePoint-as-substrate route was considered and rejected (per-org tenancy collides with the cross-org wall — ADR-0043). Grounding is untouched (library-only; the sandbox never grounds).

**External dependency (owner-driven, gates go-live not the build):** the **Microsoft CSPP application** — real-Office co-authoring cannot ship until Microsoft approves. The WOPI host (P2) is built and validated against a self-hosted dev-harness engine (Collabora / OnlyOffice) meanwhile, then pointed at Microsoft Office at approval (P3). P1 has no Microsoft dependency and ships regardless.

*P1 — DMS parity (no Microsoft dependency, ship now):* **✅ T-220–T-222 built 2026-07-26** (one verified commit per ticket; api 175/175, e2e 44/44 green). Deviations: rename is **allowed while checked out** (owner-confirmed — a title is author-owned metadata, not canonical content; the T-166 precedent), so only Replace surfaces the head-lock refusal; upload now seeds a genesis ambient revision so a fresh upload reads `v0.1` and the first replace increments to `v0.2`; the `/file` path joins `sandbox-uploads` on the CSRF multipart allowlist (ADR-0044).
- **T-220 — Contracts + API: sandbox document rename + replace-native-file.** Close the two gaps found this session: a sandbox document has no rename path (the PATCH bodies only carry `content` / `authoringMetadata`), and an uploaded file cannot be replaced. Add rename (`title`) — allowed on an unbound document; a bound document's display name stays the container's (ADR-0038). Add `POST /sandbox-documents/:id/file` (multipart) replacing the canonical native file with a new upload of the same format family — writes a new blob + `file_ref`, bumps the working revision; **refused while `head_locked`** (it rewrites canonical content, like the T-122 conversion) and only for `origin='uploaded'`. Durable prior-blob retention is P2 (noted). | *(Deps: T-122, T-166)*
- **T-221 — Surface: rename & replace-file actions in the sandbox drawer.** Per-document row/context actions in the folder view (reusing the T-163 `Modal`): **Rename** (text field) and **Replace file…** (file picker, `origin='uploaded'` only), each surfacing the head-lock refusal cleanly; the row shows format + last-updated. No `window.prompt`, semantic tokens only (the standing A2.1 acceptance tests). | *(Deps: T-220, T-163)*
- **T-222 — P1 acceptance e2e.** Upload a docx → rename it → replace it with a new docx (working revision increments, history shows it) → check out (freeze) → replace is refused while locked → release → replace succeeds. | *(Deps: T-220, T-221)*

*P2 — the WOPI host + embedded co-authoring* **(coarse — ticketed when the engine track starts).** Migration for the WOPI item/lock refs (reusing `head_locked` / `sandbox_checkout_events`) and the `file_ref` pointer extension; the WOPI host endpoints (`CheckFileInfo` / `GetFile` / `PutFile` / lock) with access gated by `sandbox_scope_grants`; `PutFile` → a `v0.x` ambient working revision (ADR-0041); the embedded editor pane in the sandbox drawer; the dev-harness engine (Collabora / OnlyOffice) provisioned as the first real infra dependency (ADR-0037 / the infra session). Acceptance: open → co-edit → save-back → new working version, plus the wall negative (revoke drops editor access in-transaction).

*P3 — CSPP → real Microsoft Office* **(coarse; gated on the CSPP approval).** Swap the P2 dev-harness engine for genuine Microsoft Office for the web behind the same WOPI host; desktop co-authoring is a later CSPP milestone.

*P4 — the Infora agent as an Office Add-in* **(coarse; converges with Slice B below).** The task-pane Add-in that grounds against the **library** from inside Office via `groundedLibrary(slice)` — the draft (read from Office.js) fused with the grounded record, in one surface. Shares its surface with Slice B's Word add-in; design not settled (ADR-0043 open item).

**Slice O — The document ontology: classification vocabulary + first-class relationships** — 🎯 **designed 2026-07-26 (ADR-0045; grill session O); Drawer 6 drawn ([data-model.md](data-model.md)); P1 ✅ built 2026-07-26 (T-240–T-244; renumbered from the drafted T-223–T-227, which collided with concurrent UI/polish commits T-223–T-233 — a T-234–T-239 gap is left for other live sessions), P2 coarse until the Engine track is live.** Built on branch `slice-o-document-ontology` in an isolated worktree (the repo had multiple live sessions); one verified commit per ticket, migration 0031, verified against an isolated DB (db 21/21, api 7/7, knowledge 26/26, e2e 7/7 incl. the wall and the plan-surface render). Over the flat library sits a legible model of *how documents relate* (component 5): a Uniclass 2015 / ISO 19650 classification vocabulary the library owner owns, and typed relationship edges between containers. Colocated relational tables, derived not duplicated (ADR-0024/0045) — so the retrieval path gains a **semantic pre-filter** in the same query as the access+state pre-filter (ADR-0022), the lever that scopes a 100k-document corpus before a single embedding is compared. Agent-facing first with a thin confirmation surface (classification an editable field, edges agent-proposed/human-confirmed — ADR-0045 Fork 3). Grounding is untouched (the ontology is metadata and structure, never a grounded corpus — ADR-0011/0021).

*P1 — the ontology substrate + retrieval pre-filter (no Engine dependency, ship now):*
- **T-240 — Data-model Drawer 6 + migration + seed: the classification vocabulary and relationship-edge tables.** Drawn (Drawer 6). Write the migration for `classification_facet`, `classification_term` (hierarchical, currency-by-state), `container_classification` (mutable, agent-proposed/human-editable), `document_relationship` (append-only, propose-then-confirm, currency-by-state). Seed Infora's default Uniclass 2015 / ISO 19650 facets + terms and **copy them per project at creation** (mirror the acceptance-code seed, ADR-0003/0045). Contracts types. | *(Deps: the acceptance-code copy-per-project seed — T-115 precedent)*
- **T-241 — Contracts + API: classify a container; propose / confirm / retire edges.** Set and edit a container's classification per facet (agent-proposed values allowed, human-editable); create an edge (proposed, no effect), confirm an edge (human-confirm → live), retire an edge (currency-by-state, never deleted). Reads: a container's classification + edges; a project's facet/term vocabulary. Access-resolved (component 2) — edges and classification ride the deliverable-visibility pre-filter (Drawer 5); no path resolves its own permissions. | *(Deps: T-240)*
- **T-242 — Retrieval: the semantic pre-filter.** Extend the grounding/retrieval query (ADR-0022/0024) so a scoped retrieval pre-filters by classification facet/term and by edge-connected containers *in the same statement* as the existing access+state pre-filter — the 100k-doc scoping lever; add the classification slice params to `groundedLibrary(slice)`. Structural-only reads (currency / coverage / dependency) answer from the tables with no vector search. | *(Deps: T-240; existing retrieval T-012/T-033/T-054)*
- **T-243 — Surface: classification field + edge confirmation in the Documents / container view.** A container's classification shown as an editable per-facet field (badged "suggested, unconfirmed" when agent-proposed); its relationship edges listed with accept / reject (confirm / retire) actions — the thin confirmation surface (Fork 3). Semantic tokens, no `window.prompt` (standing A2.1 acceptance tests). | *(Deps: T-241; the Documents view T-110)*
- **T-244 — P1 acceptance e2e.** Create a project (default scheme copied) → classify a container against a facet/term → propose an edge between two containers → confirm it (goes live) → a scoped retrieval pre-filters to the classified subset (fewer candidates than corpus-wide) → retire the edge (leaves the record, no longer counts) → the wall negative: an edge into an unshared container is invisible to a non-shared org. | *(Deps: T-240–T-243)*

*P2 — the agent's structural checks + auto-proposal* **(coarse — gated on the Engine track, component 6, and its later grill).** The agent proposes classification + edges on promotion, reconciling cross-org naming by KROMA-style ontology matching (org A's "flood study" = org B's "FRA"); the high-value checks as Engine workflows/tools — **collision** (two producers drafting to the same asset/work-package before either promotes), **coverage / lost-work** (planned MIDP containers with no linked draft; unbound sandbox docs whose classification matches a waiting container — feeds the ADR-0038 binding transition), **supersede-impact** (walk `references` edges to flag every document and past citation that grounded on a now-superseded version). A dedicated graph-explorer / ontology-management UI rides Slice G (breadth surfaces). Acceptance and tickets drawn when the Engine slice opens.

**Slice Ask — The agent harness: Ask becomes a typed-worker, planned, evaluable analysis surface** — 🎯 **discovered + specified 2026-07-29 ([docs/ask/](../ask/)); T-245–T-298 ticketed, Wave 0 part-built.** Ask today is a four-step coded chain behind a thin chat screen (T-052/T-088). This slice makes it an agent harness: seven typed workers, a persisted and editable **plan artefact**, two honestly-labelled orchestration modes, task-class model routing inside the existing ADR-0037 tier router, **Lens** personas as declarative domain content, scoping questions, Teach, and — landing early rather than last — an **eval harness** with mandatory permission cases on every build. The design layer is [docs/ask/](../ask/) (indexed by its README); the discovery report and its permission interrogation are [phase-0-discovery.md](../ask/phase-0-discovery.md). *The `docs/ask/` design documents fold into their component docs and ADRs as each area is built — see the note at the end of this slice.*

*Owner rulings, Phase 0–2 gates (2026-07-29):* **both orchestration modes ship, honestly labelled** (ADR-0027 §3 split into its classification and ordering claims — the first stands unchanged; ADR-0028 §5's named-but-not-built divergence is now built); **web-research results are citable in a separate external register** (ADR-0022 amended; user-pinned attached sources unchanged); the persona is a **Lens**, not a role (CONTEXT.md, since "role" is Membership role); the **consenting vocabulary** (NSIP/DCO/PINS/ExA/PEIR/REAC/Rochdale…) is admitted to CONTEXT.md; **Teach carries no aggregation across customers** — it improves the originating organisation's own layer only, ADR-0026 applied unchanged; the **authority corpus is two-tier** (ADR-0023 extended — Infora ships freely-shippable material, organisations add their own licensed standards into portable org context); a citation must be **checkable not merely precise** (verbatim passage where no locator is extractable); and **no user-facing orchestration-mode selector** — the Tools chip already expresses that intent.

*Wave 0 — permissions (T-245–T-254).* **✅ T-245–T-247 built 2026-07-29–30** (one verified commit per ticket, branch `slice-ask-conflict-register`; api 201/201, db 39/39, governance 64/64, full check green).
- **T-245 — Conflict register: schema and predicate.** ✅ Built. **Scope corrected 2026-07-30 —** an *administrative* guardrail checked at enrolment, not an access control: the re-check briefly added to `resolveAccess` has been removed, and ADR-0046 §3 struck. Finding F1 was rated High and is Low: the leak it reached for cannot occur, because a request runs in exactly one environment (ADR-0025). Migration 0032 + the exclusion predicate in `packages/governance`, individual grain with an optional organisation form, symmetric by construction (canonical pair, CHECK-enforced), currency-by-state. Two live partial unique indexes rather than one over a nullable subject — drizzle 0.45.2 cannot express `NULLS NOT DISTINCT`, without which duplicate organisation-grain rows are admitted. | *(ADR-0046; Deps: none)*
- **T-246 — Conflict register: refusal, retrospective report, attestation, admin surface.** ✅ Built. Migration 0033. Grant-time refusal with the fixed ADR-0046 §9 wording (`forbidden`, not `not_found` — the requester already sees both project and user); every refusal audited to its exclusion; declaring reports existing both-sides holders and revokes nothing; the owner's attestation carries no register data, asserted by pinning the payload's exact key set. Two panels in personal settings. | *(Deps: T-245)*
- **T-247 — RLS on the grounding index, source guards, and a real application role.** ✅ Built. Migration 0034. **The acceptance criterion caught the failure mode the ticket named:** policies alone returned all rows, because the dev role is a superuser and a superuser bypasses RLS entirely. Fixed by a second unprivileged `infora_app` role for the application, migrations and seed staying on the owner — which changes the first-day path (README, `.env.example`, CI). Policy fails closed; scope declared by `withProjectScope` inside `groundedLibrary`. Plus two source guards in `pnpm run check`: the `versionChunks` symbol fenced to knowledge/data, and no prompt template may carry a permission instruction. | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-248 — Scope attenuation on `EntitledSlice`.** Optional narrowing intersected into the pre-filter, never unioned; monotonic composition; the existing no-widening signature test extended to assert narrowing cannot widen either. **A hardening, not a gap, and it blocks nothing** (downgraded 2026-07-30) — escalation is already structurally impossible, and equal scope leaks nothing because every worker runs inside the caller's single environment. | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-249 — Label propagation on write-back.** 🔒 Compute the most restrictive label across a run's source set and enforce it on every write path; a destination broader than the sources is refused with both labels named; override explicit, recorded, attributed. Closes finding F2 — an answer grounded on a participant-narrowed deliverable can currently land in a multi-org sandbox. Largest risk is enumerating every write path. | *(Deps: none; blocks T-280, T-295)*
- **T-250 — The untrusted-content type barrier.** 🔒 `ExternalSource` as a type distinct from `AssembledItem` with no conversion function; a `packages/external` leaf whose manifest excludes `@infora/db` and `@infora/knowledge`, dep-rule enforced; an expected-compile-error fixture asserting the mistake is not expressible. Resolve the reserved `web` attached-source kind. Closes F3. | *(Deps: none; blocks T-279)*
- **T-251 — Session lifetime and a server-side session record.** 🔒 Absolute lifetime + idle timeout, both config; a `sessions` table so a session can be revoked, which a signed cookie alone cannot be. Closes half of F4. | *(Deps: none; blocks T-252)*
- **T-252 — Per-step slice re-resolution.** 🔒 Re-resolve the `EntitledSlice` at every plan step; a step whose re-resolution fails does not run and the run reports why it stopped. Matters once a plan fans out over minutes. | *(Deps: T-251, T-260)*
- **T-253 — Passage-grain audit.** Record `chunk_id` alongside `version_id` in `source_set`, and a producer-private read that reconstructs a run's assembled context exactly. Converts "we log what it saw" from a claim into a demonstration. | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-254 — Real cost attribution.** Provider rates per model id in deployment config, passed at leaf construction; aggregation at organisation and user grain. Closes F7 — **every step in the running app currently records a cost of exactly zero**, because the rates default to 0 and the draft leaf is bound with no options. | *(Deps: none)*

*Wave 1 — the eval harness (T-255–T-259).* Early by design: the Teach loop terminates in an eval, and the fake-router substrate already makes runs deterministic. **T-255 built 2026-07-30** (`evals/`, evals 14/14, full check green).
- **T-255 — Eval harness vertical slice.** ✅ Built 2026-07-30. ⭐ Case schema, a fixture declared as **data** with a loader that materialises it into an isolated schema, and a runner that executes **through the real HTTP API with a real session** — a runner calling internal functions tests nothing about the boundary where identity is established. One permission case, deterministic across ten runs. New workspace member `evals/` (the second harness beside `e2e/`), the one dependency-matrix entry reaching a deployable — a case must cross the boundary where identity is established. **"Isolated schema" is read as an isolated namespace, not a Postgres schema:** every migration pins `public` in its foreign keys and grants (0032, 0034), so a per-fixture schema would need the migration history rewritten; each load materialises its own organisations, users and project instead, beneath the project-scoped SQL pre-filter and T-247's RLS. Nothing unevaluable is ever a pass — an unimplemented assertion type, a Lens or mode pinned before it exists, or an unresolvable ref is an `error`. | *(Deps: T-247)*
- **T-256 — The full assertion set and set metrics.** `must_cite` / `must_not_cite` / `must_contain` / `must_not_contain` / `max_uncited_claims` (counted off the `open_world` rail outcomes, not by parsing prose) / `expect_calls` / `expect_not_called`, plus gold-passage precision and recall. Each assertion type gets a passing *and* a failing case, so a wrong implementation cannot pass both. | *(Deps: T-255)*
- **T-257 — Categories, per-category reporting, and the mode split.** The five categories (happy, negative, trap, behaviour, permission); **per category and never a single aggregate**, asserted by a test that no top-level aggregate field exists; declared and model-chosen modes always reported separately; model-graded assertions under the same independence rule as the verifier. | *(Deps: T-256)*
- **T-258 — CI tiers, hold-out, flake detection.** Smoke on every change (all permission cases + one per category and Lens, fake router), full nightly. Hold-out never emitted outside a release run, including counts. **A flaky declared-mode case fails the build; a flaky model-chosen case does not** — the honest asymmetry. | *(Deps: T-257)*
- **T-259 — The seed set.** Sixteen cases in Infora's own library on fictional fixtures. `PERM-05` (the same question under all four Lenses returns an identical source set) and `BEH-05` (promoting the draft Commercial Lens fails validation with all three named messages) protect design decisions rather than behaviour, and are the two most likely to be quietly dropped. | *(Deps: T-258)*

*Wave 2 — orchestration (T-260–T-268).* Starts from a no-behaviour-change slice. **T-260 built 2026-07-30** (migration 0035; db 46/46, orchestration 18/18, evals 15/15, full check green).
- **T-260 — The plan artefact, persisted for the existing chain.** ✅ Built 2026-07-30. ⭐ `plans` / `plan_steps` in drawer 3 (drawn first, migration 0035); every run writes a plan whose steps correspond 1:1 to its Step rows. Versioned by supersession, immutable from `ready`. **Acceptance is that the eval smoke set is byte-identical** — this ticket changes no behaviour and must prove it. **Proved:** the smoke result file before and after is identical once uuids and the generation timestamp are canonicalised (a fresh fixture instance necessarily has new ids), and the projection is now pinned as an eval test. Deviations: the 1:1 is against the run's **top-level** Step rows — the delegate step hangs beneath the retrieve step (`parent_step_id`), and a sub-agent's child run carries no plan of its own, because a delegation is not a request. `mode` is `declared` (the coded chain is pre-declared and repeatable) with `workflow_id` null until T-265; `lens_id` null until T-281; `restatement` null until the classifier at T-266 — each recorded as absent rather than invented. **Also fixed a shared-database race the eval harness exposed:** `ingestVersions` walks every version in the database and replaces its chunks wholesale, so a fixture sharing `fake-embed` could be re-chunked underneath a running case; eval fixtures now write their own pinned index (`eval-embed`, ADR-0024). | *(Deps: T-255)*
- **T-261 — Plan read API and permissions.** Producer-private, resolved through `resourceScope`; a different organisation gets the same 404 as nonexistence; edit-and-rerun restricted to the requesting Participant. | *(Deps: T-260)*
- **T-262 — Execute from the plan.** The executor walks `plan.steps` honouring `depends_on`, replacing the hard-coded sequence. **The ground-check must stay outside the plan** — if it becomes a plan step a planner could skip it, which breaks the guarantee both modes rest on; asserted by a test. | *(Deps: T-260)*
- **T-263 — Step and run state migration.** `step_type` gains the worker step types; `run_state` gains `completed_with_failures`; a test asserts the contracts types and the DB enum cannot drift. | *(Deps: T-262)*
- **T-264 — Workflow DAG format, loader and validator.** `packages/workflows` is an empty stub today. Validation at load: every worker in the registry, acyclic, resolvable `depends_on`, **no step may declare a scope** (inherited and not expressible), `writes` declaring its label-propagation behaviour, drafts non-production only. Each rule gets a fixture that fails it. | *(Deps: T-263)*
- **T-265 — `workflow_runner` and the first declared workflow.** The existing four-step chain declared as a DAG, changing no behaviour. The one non-leaf worker; keeping it from becoming a general escape hatch is review discipline, not a test. | *(Deps: T-264, T-269)*
- **T-266 — Model-chosen orchestration and mode labelling.** Classification into four outcomes; the dispatch loop over the **entitled** worker set. **Ground-check runs on every answer in both modes**, asserted for a plan that does not declare it. Mode on the plan, the run, Teach submissions and the footer. Largest risk is classification quality — a weak classifier routes everything to model-chosen and the product quietly becomes the generic agent the design forbids, which is why the fall-through rate is a reported metric. | *(Deps: T-265)*
- **T-267 — Plan edit and re-run.** Supersession, not mutation. **An edited plan is `model_chosen` even if it started `declared`** — a hand-edited workflow is no longer the declared workflow, and the UI says so at the point of editing. | *(Deps: T-266)*
- **T-268 — Partial failure semantics.** Failed step → dependants skipped, independent branches continue, `completed_with_failures` when output survived. **The answer body reports what did not run**, not only the footer — absence detection applied to the system's own failures. | *(Deps: T-266)*

*Wave 3 — workers (T-269–T-280).* Two spikes start immediately and block nothing in Wave 0.
- **T-269 — Worker registry, typed contract, entitlement assembly.** ⭐ The declaration type plus one worker (`corpus_retrieval`). **The tool set is assembled from entitlements, not filtered** — an unentitled worker is absent, not disabled, and the model is never told it exists. A sovereign-tier deployment assembles no `web_research`, falling out of the existing router policy. | *(Deps: T-248, T-263)*
- **T-270 — SPIKE: locator extraction.** The chunker records no page/paragraph/section, so citations resolve at version grain. Per format: what locator is reliably extractable, and where the **verbatim-passage fallback** applies (owner-ruled). The open engineering case is a quote spanning a chunk boundary. | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-271 — Locators through the ingest pipeline.** Locator capture persisted on `version_chunks` and carried to the rendered citation, plus the verbatim fallback. **The quoted passage must be findable in the source document** — a quote that cannot be found is worse than none, because it looks checkable. | *(Deps: T-270)*
- **T-272 — `corpus_retrieval`: coverage note, chunk ids, structured output.** 🔒 The `coverage_note` states what was searched and what found nothing — the mechanism behind absence detection. **The cache key includes the scope hash**; a cache without scope in the key is a permission bypass with extra steps. | *(Deps: T-269, T-253)*
- **T-273 — `include_superseded` with mandatory flagging.** Default exclusion unchanged. A superseded source carries a flag **in the prose at the point of use**, not only in the manifest — easy to render in the footer and easy to forget where it matters. | *(Deps: T-272)*
- **T-274 — `extractor` and the named schemas.** Commitments, consultee responses, mitigation measures, ExA questions, deadlines, parameters, as versioned domain content beside the Lens files. `strict` defaults true and `failures` is a first-class output — **a silently coerced commitment is worse than no record**. | *(Deps: T-269)*
- **T-275 — `verifier` on an independent model family.** Per-claim verdicts **on top of** the deterministic ground-check, never instead of it — asserted by a test that removes the verifier from a plan and finds ground-check still ran. Where no independent family conforms to the tier, verification is **unavailable and skipped with a stated reason**, never silently same-family. | *(Deps: T-269, T-286)*
- **T-276 — SPIKE: the authority corpus.** `authorityRef` runs through contracts, the citation table and the ground-check, but there is no store — the canon half of Ask has no data. Licensing is ruled (two-tier); the spike names the v1 standard-tier instrument list with a licence basis for each, the in-force interval model, and org-tier ingest. | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-277 — Authority corpus store and ingest.** 🔒 Both tiers. A query for a past `in_force_at` returns the version in force **at that date**. **An organisation's tier is invisible to every other organisation** — a wall test, not merely a scoping one. Org-tier entries cannot be recorded as Infora-maintained. | *(Deps: T-276)*
- **T-278 — `authority_lookup`.** 🔒 Standard tier ∪ the requester's own organisation tier, per-tier currency note, cache keyed on `org_shelf_version` — a cache keyed only on the query would serve one firm's private shelf to another. | *(Deps: T-277, T-269)*
- **T-279 — `web_research`.** 🔒 In `packages/external` behind the T-250 barrier: no `Db`, no `assemble`, no `EntitledSlice`, proven by the dep rule. Corpus content never present in its context, asserted by inspecting its actual inputs. User-pinned web attached sources remain non-citing — the two halves of the ADR-0022 amendment. | *(Deps: T-250, T-269)*
- **T-280 — `document_builder`.** 🔒 Draft into a template with a source manifest and the computed label enforced against the destination. `sources` is explicit — the builder does not retrieve, which keeps the label computation tractable and the manifest honest. | *(Deps: T-249, T-269)*

*Wave 4 — Lens (T-281–T-283).* Surface-and-prompt only; independently shippable.
- **T-281 — `packages/lenses`: loader, validator, one Lens wired.** ⭐ A leaf package depending on `contracts` only; definitions move verbatim from `docs/ask/lenses/`. **A Lens whose prohibitions try to weaken a shared-core rule fails to load**, with a message naming file, field and rule in language a domain expert can act on — error-message quality decides whether this layer stays domain-expert-owned. **The Lens is not a parameter of `resolveAccess`, `assemble` or `groundedLibrary`**, asserted by a signature test. | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-282 — The four active Lenses and the draft.** Planning & Environmental, Engineer, Project Manager, Communications, plus the deliberately-incomplete Commercial. Each Lens's worked exchanges become behaviour eval cases — the guard against register differences being cosmetic. | *(Deps: T-281)*
- **T-283 — Lens switching, persistence, logging.** Switching re-renders the next answer only; history keeps the Lens that produced it. Default is config, not code. | *(Deps: T-282)*

*Wave 5 — model routing (T-284–T-286).*
- **T-284 — Task-class routing.** `Router.chat(task, …)` accepts a task argument and currently ignores it — the seam exists, the routing does not. **Tier conformance applies before task selection**, unchanged; the ordering is easy to invert when adding the second axis. | *(Deps: T-263)*
- **T-285 — Fallback chains.** A fallback is attempted only if it also conforms to the deployment tier; availability is never traded for conformance. Every attempt, including failures, writes a Step audit row with egress facts. | *(Deps: T-284)*
- **T-286 — The verify independence constraint.** Enforced in code, not only expressed in config — a config naming the producing family fails at dispatch. | *(Deps: T-284)*

*Wave 6 — scoping questions (T-287–T-288).* Labelled **Scoping**, not "clarify" — a step planners already recognise.
- **T-287 — Clarification schema, plan states, binding.** Answers bind into the plan; **skipping all proceeds on stated assumptions named at the top of the answer**, not in a footer. **No question offers an option the user cannot reach** — a scoping question is about relevance, never permission. | *(Deps: T-266)*
- **T-288 — The scoping surface.** Paginated, position indicator, at most one RECOMMENDED badge, Custom, Skip, and Skip All never buried. **Every option's info affordance states a consequence, not a definition** — the difference between a colleague and a glossary. | *(Deps: T-287)*

*Wave 7 — Teach (T-289–T-291).* Everything lands inside the originating organisation.
- **T-289 — Teach capture.** 🔒 The dialogue states in plain words that the text stays inside the organisation; the checkbox asks the question that actually matters — *safe to reuse on this organisation's other projects* (ADR-0026 Filter 2), not "confidential". **No submission field leaves the organisation**, asserted over the write path. | *(Deps: T-266)*
- **T-290 — The reviewer queue.** 🔒 Organisation-facing, for the firm's own curator. **Promotion takes a required, non-nullable approving participant id** — no `autoApprove` flag, config key or environment variable, proven by grep. Content can be removed, not only added. | *(Deps: T-289)*
- **T-291 — Correction → organisation eval case.** Into that organisation's own library, pinned to its own fixture. **The new case is run at conversion and a case that passes is closed as noise** — without that gate the suite inflates with cases that can never catch a regression. | *(Deps: T-290, T-259)*

*Wave 8 — interface (T-292–T-296).*
- **T-292 — Composer chips.** Lens, Model, Data sources, Tools, Context. The Lens picker states in the picker that a Lens does not change what you can see. The Model chip lists only tier-conforming routes. **The Data sources chip warns when zero sources are in scope**, and refinement narrows only, intersected server-side. | *(Deps: T-283, T-284)*
- **T-293 — The progress rail.** Driven by plan step states, **never a client-side timer** — a timer-driven rail looks right most of the time, which is what makes it a trust problem rather than a bug. A stage that did not run is never shown as having run. | *(Deps: T-268)*
- **T-294 — The completion footer and plan view.** The orchestration mode stated **in words**, always visible; the Lens and version; Details exposing the plan, workers, per-step cost with pins marked, and the citation manifest. | *(Deps: T-267, T-293)*
- **T-295 — The output destination selector.** 🔒 A destination broader than the source material warns naming both labels and is blocked by default. Cannot ship before T-249 — a selector without propagation implies a guarantee the backend does not make. | *(Deps: T-249, T-280)*
- **T-296 — Four-register rendering.** Record, Inference, Authority and External **visually distinct by chip shape and colour, not by tooltip**. A reader skim-reading must tell a web source from a project document without hovering — the visible half of the ADR-0022 carve-out, and the half a client will judge. | *(Deps: T-279, T-278, T-271)*

*Raised during the build:*
- **T-297 — RLS on `containers`.** Split from T-247: `version_chunks` has two non-test consumers so its scope declares inside one function, while `containers` has thirteen across the API, each needing transaction scoping. A refactor with its own risk profile; wants the same per-request seam as Wave 2. | *(Deps: T-247)*
- **T-298 — Seed the conflict-register scenario; deterministic participant order.** ✅ Built 2026-07-30. A second client and scheme, so an exclusion has two projects to pair; `readMe` ordered by `created_at` because twelve e2e specs index `participants[0]`. **Fixed a T-247 regression:** under RLS a DELETE must first *find* its rows through the SELECT policy, so ingest's replace-wholesale step deleted nothing and re-insert collided — ingest had become silently non-idempotent. The existing test would have caught it, but turbo had **cached** `@infora/data`'s result from before the migration; turbo keys on file hashes and cannot see database state. | *(Deps: T-245, T-247)*

*Where the design documents end up:* `docs/ask/` holds the Phase 1 specification while the slice is being built. Each document folds into its component doc or an ADR as its area lands — Lens and workers into component 6, routing into component 1, scoping and interface into component 8, Teach into component 4, permissions into component 2, the eval harness into `docs/build/`. The folder shrinks to nothing rather than being migrated in one go, so the fold happens when content has settled. [phase-0-discovery.md](../ask/phase-0-discovery.md) stays as a dated report.

**Slice B — The Word add-in** *(design settled, component 8; converges with Slice A3 P4).* The consultant authoring surface: tracked-changes suggestions with citation + rationale, accept/edit/reject as Signals, central M365 deployment. Needs Slice A's promotion path to be fully useful, but drafting on sandbox documents can land earlier.

**Slice C — Governance depth** *(part open: threshold tuning, retention/export — bucket A).* Rails as scoped records with the ADR-0030 intersection engine, grounding-threshold calibration, withheld-output UX, audit retention/export, user-UI-action audit sense.

**Slice D — Retrieval maturity** *(gate: Session 6 finish).* Contextual retrieval ("x in the context of y"), real channel ranking and budget, org-vs-programme precedence, per-viewer citation rendering — behind the unchanged ADR-0029 signature.

**Slice E — The moat loop** *(gate: Sessions 4, 5, 7 — must-grill, the cross-org confidentiality forks).* Org/programme context stores and drawers, the distillation engine with the ADR-0026 destination rule, precedent selection, the Signal sink, guidance notes (ADR pending), and the ADR-0026 within-tenant/cross-tenant training reconciliation flagged in the tracker.

**Slice F — Build-your-own** *(gate: Engine §5 opens — builder interface, tightening validation, sharing).* Custom tools (the Tools surface, T-109) and org-built agents: authoring through the builder in Tools, org-context storage, deploy-time rails inheritance, pre-deploy validation. The tool-scoping ruling (2026-07-13) and the wall-clean-definition stress test are on the tracker's builder theme.

**Slice G — Breadth surfaces** *(bucket A, reference-decidable).* Workspace home vs project home layout, the owner/client portfolio "control tower", programme views, mobile scope.

**Slice H — Connectors** *(deferred until the wedge is proven).* Integrate-configuration handover to an incumbent DMS; spatial/CAD/BIM by reference.

**Gate before any external pilot — the infra/security decision session** *(bucket C, component 1).* Cloud provider, blob/object storage for renditions, hosting and deployment, encryption and key management, tenant isolation, residency, production identity (replacing the skeleton auth above). The skeleton deliberately runs on the dev substrate until this is held.
